The serR/desR field map is a CLEAN BIJECTION, unlike the several serP/desP write/read asymmetries C21c/C21d documented: every key `serR` emits (`isRaster`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `opacity`, `isBitmapBrush`, `linked`, `linkedPath`, `linkedHandleId`, `src`, `rotation`, `brushGroupId`, `isBrushTextureCopy`, `meshId`, `groupId`, `isText`, `text`, `font`, `size`, `color`, `align`, `fixedWidth`, `isTextChar`, `textGroupId`, `charIndex`, `wordIndex`, `lineIndex`) is read by `desR` (directly, or — for `isRaster` — by desR's own EXTERNAL callers as the discriminator that decides whether to call `desR` at all, app.js:4795/tweens.js:4748-4749/export.js:239/labs+storyboard call sites below), and no field `desR` reads (app.js:1196-1250) is absent from `serR`'s own emission set (app.js:1036-1121) — confirmed by manual enumeration of every `d.<field>` read in `desR`'s body against every field name in `serR`'s own return-object construction, cross-checked both directions. The two exceptions are not stored fields at all: `op` (desR's third formal parameter, a caller-supplied opacity OVERRIDE with no corresponding key in `d` — same shape as C21d's own `desP` `op` parameter finding) and the two live-object-only communication tags `r.data._pendingGeom` (written by `desR` at line 1227, read only by `serR` at line 1048, cleared by `desR`'s own `place()` at line 1231 — never part of the persisted dict `d` itself) and `r.data.linkedMissing` (written by `desR` at line 1218 when a linked source can't be resolved synchronously; `serR` never reads or re-emits it).

`r.data.linkedMissing` (app.js:1218) has ZERO readers anywhere else in `src/js` at this SHA — confirmed by `git grep -n 'linkedMissing' 59a5a38c -- src/js` returning only its own write site. Either a dead write, or a UI hook (e.g. a broken-link badge on a linked-media layer) that was planned but never wired at this SHA; not reproduced or fixed here.

`op` parameter semantics mirror `desP`'s own `op` (C21d, cited by line only): `r.opacity=op!==undefined?op:(d.opacity!==undefined?d.opacity:1);` (app.js:1222) — the formal parameter takes priority over the stored `d.opacity`, which itself defaults to `1` only when BOTH are undefined. Of the scope's 9 confirmed call sites (see the `desr` packet's own `callers`), exactly ONE passes an explicit `op` — export.js:239 (`sd.isRaster?desR(sd,L,sd.opacity!==undefined?sd.opacity:1):desP(...)`, inside `exportBuildFrame`'s per-stroke `forEach`) — the other 8 call sites are 2-argument calls, so `op` is always `undefined` there and `desR` falls through to `d.opacity`. tweens.js's onion-skin renderer (`renderOS`, lines 4748-4749) uses a THIRD pattern: it calls `desR(sd,onionPrevLayer)` with no third argument, then overwrites the returned Raster's `.opacity` directly (`pr.opacity=op;`/`nr.opacity=op2;`) AFTER the call — bypassing the `op` parameter entirely rather than passing the onion-skin fade fraction through it.

The `isRaster` discriminator has TWO distinct manifestations, not one code path: (1) a DICT-LEVEL boolean flag on a persisted stroke dict, read by `getEffectiveStrokes` (app.js:2949, reads at 3059/3092), `loadFrame` (app.js:4746, reads at 4795), `applyMatrixToStrokeData` (app.js:1329, reads at 1330/1437 — the latter inside `_boundsCenterOfStrokes`, app.js:1434), `_normStrokeForCompare` (app.js:4437, reads at 4487), `splitFrame` (app.js:5070, reads at 5074/5084), export.js (`exportBuildFrame`, reads at 189/198/202/218/239/248/268/1115) and tweens.js (`splitTweenables`/onion-skin/others, reads at 3634/3663/3674/4586/4748/4749); (2) a LIVE `instanceof Raster` check on the actual Paper.js item, used by `buildSceneJson` (engine-bridge.js:1441, 2694 — cite by line only, engine-bridge.js territory) and by this scope's own `serR` caller `_collectLayerStrokes` (app.js:4563, branch at 4574: `else if(c instanceof Raster)strokes.push(serR(c));`). The two never need to agree with each other directly — the dict flag is manufactured BY `serR` FROM the live-object check — but a future consumer reading `sd.isRaster` on a hand-built dict that skipped `serR` would not be covered by this equivalence.

Image-cache contract, verified by direct read (app.js:1131-1195): key is the raster's data: URL string itself (`src`, the same value `serR`/`desR` round-trip as `d.src`); caps are `_imgCacheMax=120` entries AND `_imgCacheMaxBytes=192*1024*1024` (192MB, approximated as `src.length` — the base64 STRING length, not decoded pixel bytes) — `_imgCachePut` (app.js:1181-1191) evicts OLDEST-FIRST (`_imgCache.keys().next()`, a `Map` preserves insertion order) in a `while` loop until BOTH caps are satisfied, after every insert; `_imgCacheGet` (app.js:1157-1165) re-inserts a hit (`delete` then `set`) to mark it most-recently-used, so the eviction order is LRU by last-GET-or-PUT, not pure insertion order despite the comment's own 'LRU by insertion order' phrasing — re-insertion on read IS the LRU mechanism.

The lead-in's own claim (app.js:1140-1143: 'Every path that CHANGES a raster's pixels — eraseBite, flushEraseDirty, liveRestamp, regenerate — writes a fresh toDataURL string...a mutated image can never read a stale entry') is VERIFIED TRUE IN EFFECT but OVER-ATTRIBUTED TO ALL FOUR names: direct read of bitmap-brush.js shows only `flushEraseDirty` (bitmap-brush.js:514-521, `c.data.src=c.canvas.toDataURL('image/png')`) and `regenerate`'s own downstream call into `applyBitmapBrushTexture` (which itself calls `toDataURL` at bitmap-brush.js:525) actually mint a fresh string key. `eraseBite` (bitmap-brush.js:493-512) and `liveRestamp` (bitmap-brush.js:462-478) mutate `raster.canvas` pixels DIRECTLY and explicitly do NOT call `toDataURL` — bitmap-brush.js's own comments state this is deliberate ('data.src...intentionally NOT refreshed per bite', 'NO toDataURL — the persistable data.src is only refreshed by the full regenerate() at drag end'), to avoid a synchronous encode per pointermove. The invariant still holds in EFFECT in current code because `_imgCacheGet`/`desR` are only consulted at Raster RECONSTRUCTION time (a fresh `desR` call, e.g. during `loadFrame`/onion-skin/export), never against the SAME live object mid-drag — no code path in this scope reads the cache against a raster whose canvas has been mutated but whose `data.src` has not yet been refreshed. The claim is therefore correct about the OUTCOME (no stale read is observable) but imprecise about the MECHANISM (2 of the 4 named functions defer the key refresh rather than performing it inline).

`_imgCacheWarm`'s own async decode (app.js:1172-1179) is guarded by `_imgCacheWarming[src]` (app.js:1173, checked; 1174, set) so a second `desR` call for the SAME still-decoding `src` (e.g. two rasters sharing one image within the same `loadFrame` pass) does not start a second `Image()` decode — `_imgCacheGet` reports a miss for a pending entry regardless (line 1164's `.complete&&.naturalWidth` check), so the caller always falls through to the synchronous `new Raster(srcForRaster)` path (app.js:1216) for that raster while the warm decode races in the background for the NEXT `desR` call on the same key; the guard is cleared in both the `onload`/`onerror` handlers (app.js:1176/1177) so a failed decode can be retried on a later call.

None of the six decoded-image-cache symbols (`_imgCacheMax`/`_imgCacheMaxBytes`/`_imgCache`/`_imgCacheBytes`/`_imgCacheGet`/`_imgCacheWarm`/`_imgCacheWarming`/`_imgCachePut`/`_imgCacheHits`/`_imgCacheMisses` — the issue's own packet table names six but the module actually declares ten identifiers across those six roles, see the `image-cache` packet's own `symbols` list) has any caller OUTSIDE app.js itself at this SHA — confirmed by `git grep -n '_imgCache' 59a5a38c -- . ':!src/js/app.js'`, whose only hits are reference-bridge.js's unrelated same-named field (see `reconciliation` above) and comments in linked-media.js/a census artifact. Within app.js, the ONLY caller of `_imgCacheGet`/`_imgCacheWarm` is `desR` itself (lines 1214-1215); `_imgCacheWarm` is the only caller of `_imgCachePut` (line 1176); `window.__imgCacheStats`/`window.__imgCacheReset` (lines 1193-1194) are the only readers of `_imgCacheHits`/`_imgCacheMisses` outside `desR`'s own increment at line 1215, and have no caller anywhere in `src/js` at this SHA either (exposed for external/console-driven measurement only, per their own comment). This CORRECTS the issue's own hinted expectation ('expect... images.js/media-library.js/video bridges — complete file:line'): no such calls exist. images.js:418 is a `//`-comment MENTIONING `desR()`, not a call to it or to any cache symbol; media-library.js and native-video-bridge.js contain no reference to `desR`, `serR`, or any `_imgCache*` symbol at all.

The onLoad-after-construction race (app.js:1122-1130's own lead-in) is handled at THREE independent sites, not one: (1) `desR`'s own `onLoad` hook (app.js:1233-1249) re-renders via `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` once decode completes, to self-heal a scrub that outran the decode; (2) `serR`'s own `_pendingGeom` synchronous fallback (app.js:1037-1048) reads the INTENDED geometry `desR` stashed synchronously, for the case where `serR` is asked to re-serialize a still-`!r.loaded` Raster (the bug #9 mid-decode race); (3) images.js's video-frame importer (`importVideoFrames`, images.js:403-427) awaits `r.on('load',...)` with an explicit 1.5s timeout fallback BEFORE calling `saveAllLayerFrames()` (via `convertLayerToComponent`), guarding the SAME underlying async-decode concern from the caller side of `loadFrame`/`desR` rather than from inside either function — confirmed this is a THIRD, independent guard (not a call into `desR`'s own `onLoad` or `serR`'s own `_pendingGeom`) by direct read.

packets.responsibility: Serializes one live Paper.js `Raster` (an imported image, video frame, baked bitmap-brush texture, baked text block, or split text character) into a plain persistable dict, applying a mid-decode geometry fallback (`_pendingGeom`) and a rotation-aware size decomposition before emitting the position/size/opacity core, then additively emitting every optional tag a raster may carry on its live `.data` — linked-media reference, brush-texture companion linkage, image-mesh id, group membership, and the full text-tool field set — each independently gated on its own truthy check.
callers: src/js/app.js:4574 — `_collectLayerStrokes(li,ld)` (app.js:4563-4576), the branch `else if(c instanceof Raster)strokes.push(serR(c));` inside its own `forEach` over `userLayers[li].children`. `_collectLayerStrokes` itself is called from FOUR sites, none of which pass extra arguments to the `serR` call itself (the branch takes only `c`): app.js:4689 (`saveActiveLayerFrame`, app.js:4634-4692 — the current frame's own re-serialize, CLAUDE.md §1's 'le plus critique' consumer), app.js:4707 (`saveAllLayerFrames`, app.js:4693-...), app.js:4909/4911 (`setElemHidden`, app.js:4881-..., the held-origin and keyframe/interpolated-frame re-serialize branches after an eye/solo toggle), and app.js:4983 (`saveActiveLayerFrameOrPromote`, app.js:4969-...).
behavior: Lines 1025-1035 (comment, 11 lines): the bitmap-import lead-in — a Raster round-trips as a self-contained data: URL plus explicit x/y/width/height (re-applied on load since decode is async and may transiently report natural size). States `isBitmapBrush` round-trips through this same path as a plain import, citing CLAUDE.md §1's family-of-bug-#1 (a tag handled at the write site but forgotten at the read site).

Lines 1036-1047 (declaration + comment, 12 lines): `function serR(r){` — one formal parameter, the live Paper.js `Raster` to serialize. Documents 'bug #9' (2026-07): a Raster built by `desR` mid-scrub may still be `!r.loaded` when `saveAllLayerFrames()` re-serializes it (goToFrame saves the LEFT frame before navigating) — reading `r.position`/`r.bounds` at that moment returns the pre-resize placeholder geometry, producing a spurious divergence from stored frame data that `_maybePromoteInterpolated()` (app.js, outside this scope, cited by name only) misreads as a real edit, permanently flipping an untouched tween in-between to `isKeyframe:true`. `desR` stashes the INTENDED geometry on `r.data._pendingGeom` synchronously (before its own async gap) precisely so this fallback has something correct to read.

Line 1048 (code): `var pending=r.data&&r.data._pendingGeom;` — reads the live tag `desR` wrote (app.js:1227) and `desR`'s own `place()` clears (app.js:1231); no default, `pending` is simply `undefined`/falsy once decode has completed and `place()` has run.

Lines 1049-1059 (comment 1049-1054, code 1055-1059): rotation-aware sizing (2026-07) — once the select tool's rotate ring has spun a Raster, `r.bounds` is the INFLATED axis-aligned envelope; the honest display size is the un-rotated natural size times `|scaling|`. `rot=(!r.loaded&&pending)?(pending.rotation||0):((r.matrix&&r.matrix.rotation)||0);` — reads `pending.rotation` (default `0`) when mid-decode, else the live matrix's own rotation (default `0` via the `||0`, e.g. an un-rotated Raster). `useX`/`useY`/`useW`/`useH` follow the SAME `(!r.loaded&&pending)?pending.<field>:<live read>` ternary shape, with the live-read branch for width/height itself branching on `rot`: `rot?Math.abs(r.scaling.x)*r.width:r.bounds.width` (and the `.y`/`.height` mirror) — an un-rotated Raster keeps the historical `r.bounds` read untouched; a rotated one uses natural size × |scaling| instead of the inflated bounds.

Line 1060 (code, the densest line in this packet): `var d={isRaster:true,x:useX,y:useY,width:useW,height:useH,opacity:r.opacity!==undefined?r.opacity:1};if(r.data&&r.data.isBitmapBrush)d.isBitmapBrush=true;` — `isRaster:true` is ALWAYS emitted (the discriminator this scope's `boundaries` finding documents both manifestations of); `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` are ALWAYS emitted from the `use*` locals just derived; `opacity` is ALWAYS emitted, default `1` when `r.opacity` is undefined; `isBitmapBrush` is emitted ONLY when truthy on `r.data` (condition: `r.data&&r.data.isBitmapBrush`), a boolean literal `true` (not a passthrough of the source value), else the key is absent entirely.

Lines 1061-1077 (comment 1061-1070, code 1071-1077): linked media (2026-08-29) — when `r.data.linked` is truthy, `d.linked=true` and `d.linkedPath`/`d.linkedHandleId` are each emitted ONLY if truthy on `r.data` (both may be absent if neither backend field is set, though in practice exactly one is per `linked-media.js`'s own `keyFor`); `d.src` is DELIBERATELY OMITTED on this branch so the base64 payload never round-trips into the saved JSON — the entire weight win of linked mode. On the ELSE branch (not linked), `d.src=r.data&&r.data.src?r.data.src:r.source;` is always emitted, preferring the in-memory `r.data.src` (kept fresh by every pixel-mutating path, see `image-cache`'s own `boundaries` finding) over Paper's own `r.source` (the original construction argument, which for a `new Raster(dataURLstring)` is the same string but for a `new Raster()` element-based construction would be the element itself, not a string — not observed as a live hazard in this census, since `desR` (this scope's own `desr` packet) always constructs from a string/decoded ``/`Size`, never a bare element from outside this pair).
Line 1078 (code): `if(rot)d.rotation=rot;` — emitted only when the just-computed `rot` local is truthy (non-zero); absent (default: no rotation) when `rot===0`.

Lines 1079-1085 (comment 1079-1083, code 1084-1085): companion linkage (bitmap-brush.js's v2 anchor+companion architecture) — `d.brushGroupId` emitted only if truthy on `r.data`; `d.isBrushTextureCopy` emitted as boolean literal `true` only if truthy on `r.data`. This is the id `relinkBrushCompanions` (C21d's own scope, cited by line only) regroups a texture Raster with its anchor Path by, after `desR`/`desP` rebuild everything fresh on `loadFrame`.

Lines 1086-1094 (comment 1086-1093, code 1094): image mesh (2026-08-30) — `d.meshId` emitted only if truthy on `r.data`; deliberately the ONLY mesh-related field on the stroke dict (the mesh geometry itself lives in `state.imageMeshes`, per CLAUDE.md §12's own note that this dict is duplicated per-frame and the mesh must not be).
